department: Civil Engineering (Ph.D.), College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing

deadline.value: College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing has rolling admissions year-round; Feb 1 complete application required for Knights of Columbus / Board of Trustees scholarship nomination, and international graduate admissions lists July 1 for Fall.
deadline.quote: Graduate programs have rolling admissions and are accepted year-round.

also.quote: Deans and department chairs nominate the most qualified applicants whose application is complete by Feb. 1 for the University-wide competition for the Knights of Columbus Fellowship and the prestigious Board of Trustees full-tuition scholarship.
Application Deadlines Spring: November 1 Fall: July 1

gre_subject.value: ETS offers no GRE Subject Test in this field (Subject Tests exist only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: CEPC encourages doctoral applicants to review college research areas, identify potential dissertation advisors, and discuss research interests with faculty members when seeking RAs.
supervisor.quote: Applicants are encouraged to review the areas of research described on the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing website and to identify one or more potential doctoral dissertation advisors who have relevant research interests.

also.quote: For research assistantships, we encourage prospective students to check our faculty profiles and discuss their research interests with the faculty members whose research areas match the student's interests.

funding.value: Departments in CEPC offer competitive TA and RA positions (with PhD students given higher priority) providing full or partial tuition scholarship and a living stipend, plus Feb 1 competitive merit fellowships.
funding.quote: Each of the departments at the College of Engineering, Physics, and Computing offers teaching and research assistantships. These positions are competitive, based on academic background, GPA, research / teaching experience and potential, standard tests scores such as GRE scores and TOEFL scores. In addition, PhD students are given higher priority for consideration.

also.quote: Teaching Assistants receive a full or partial tuition scholarship and a stipend for living expenses... Research Assistants receive a full tuition scholarship and a stipend for living expenses

entry_route.value: CEPC states students are typically admitted to a doctoral program after completing a master's degree in the same field; exceptional bachelor's holders may be admitted directly while completing master's requirements en route.
entry_route.quote: Students are typically admitted to a doctoral program after completing a master's degree in the same field. In exceptional cases, a student may be admitted to a doctoral program directly with only a bachelor's degree, but will still need to complete master's degree requirements as part of the doctoral degree process.

gre_general.value: GRE is required for doctoral applicants and most university scholarships, but may be waived by College/department for published work or professional experience.
gre_general.quote: Yes for doctoral applicants, and GRE scores are necessary to be considered for most university scholarships. The requirement may be waived where the College or department finds other evidence of proficiency, such as published work or substantial professional experience.

notes: Minimum 3.4 GPA for doctoral admission; 53 credits (up to 24 transferable from another institution's MS or 30 from CUA). GRE may be waived with evidence of proficiency.
